newsitem.title: USA: Storm delays La. Offshore Oil Port crude cargo.
newsitem.headline: Storm delays La. Offshore Oil Port crude cargo.

text.p: A 900,000 barrel crude cargo due to arrive at the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port on Friday was delayed as Tropical Storm Danny bore down on the U.S. Gulf coastline, a spokesman said.
"It's delayed until we get manned and ready to go again," spokesman Dale Rollins said.
The LOOP, the only deepwater oil port in the Gulf of Mexico, continued to operate its onshore facilities but evacuated its platform lying in the track of the storm.
No cargoes were due to arrive on Thursday at the platform, which is 20 miles south of Grand Isle, La.
Danny was on track to make landfall late Thursday or early Friday, and a tropical storm warning and hurricane watch were raised from Cameron, La., to Orange Beach in east Alabama.
Houston-based Wilkens Weather Technologies was predicting landfall south of Port Fourchon, La., about 12 miles from Grand Isle.
